questions.q: Which of the following molecule has the maximum dipole moment?
questions.solution:
The dipole moment depends on the charge and distance between the central atom and side atoms. But the charge is more prominent than distance. It is determined as polar and non-polar molecules. It can be determined by the geometry of the molecule.

In case of NCl3 & NH3 the electronegativity difference between N-H is higher than the electronegativity difference between N-Cl bond so the shared pair of electrons shifted towards chlorine in case of NCl3 and in case of NH3 it will be towards Nitrogen. So, for NH3 the net dipole moment will be towards the direction of lone pair and will be added up into the dipole moment of lone pair while in case of NCl3 the moment due to three bond pairs will be in opposite direction to the dipole moment of the lone pair, and it will be subtracted results in lower value of net dipole moment.

In case of CS2, it has the linear shape and so their moment is balanced and so net dipole moment is zero.

In case of ethane C2H6, the electronegativity difference between carbon and hydrogen is minimal so unbranched alkanes have zero dipole moment. 

Hence, NH3 has maximum dipole moment among the given options.

The force exerted by gas molecules per unit area is the pressure, the gas molecules will exert more force if they have more kinetic energy and the rate of the number of collisions of gas molecules per unit area will increase the momentum transfer which again leads to increase in kinetic energy.

Therefore, pressure is directly proportional to the kinetic energy of gas molecules.

The expression for a horizontal range of a projectile is, R=u2sin2θg here, θ is the angle of projection and u is the initial resultant velocity.

For the maximum kinetic energy, the velocity should be maximum, now the velocity of the projectile is u=ux2+uy2

In the expression of the velocity of particle during projectile, the horizontal component of velocity is constant, i.e., ux=constant therefore, net velocity depends upon the vertical component of velocity, i.e., u2∝uy2 or u2cosθ

Therefore, when uy is maximum then the net velocity will be maximum and so is the kinetic energy.

Since, uy is maximum at the beginning and at the end of the flight of projectile, at the end of the flight of projectile the particle has already covered its horizontal range, therefore, kinetic energy will be maximum after covering a distance of 100 m.

questions.q: The bob of a simple pendulum is a spherical hollow ball filled with water. A plugged hole near the bottom of the oscillating bob gets suddenly unplugged. During observation, till water is coming out, the time period of oscillation would:
options: first increase and then decrease to the original value.
first decrease and then increase to the original value.
questions.solution:
The time period of the simple pendulum is, T=2πlg Here, l is the effective length of the pendulum up to centre of mass.

When the hole at bottom of the hollow sphere (bob) filled with water is unplugged, the water will drain from the bob due to which the centre of mass will shift downward, therefore, the length of the pendulum will slightly increase, which will lead to increase in time period.

After the water completely drained out the centre of mass again shift to its original position that is up to the centre of the hollow sphere (bob) due to which the length of the pendulum will decrease and will reach to its initial state which causes the time period to reach its original value.

questions.q: Boiling water is changing into steam. The specific heat of boiling water is
questions.solution:
Specific heat of any substance is the amount of heat transfer Q required to cause a unit rise in temperature ∆T of a unit mass of that substance of mass m.

s=Qm∆T

When boiling water changes into steam there is latent heat involved cause its a phase change process, during the phase change process there is no temperature change, therefore, ∆T=0

Thus, the specific heat of boiling water undergoing through phase change is s=Qm∆T=Qm×0=∞
